subject: WhiteBirch pilot: residency, hosting tiers, and cross-region routing clarification
body:
From: Sofie Berg <sofie@whitebirch.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: magnus@whitebirch.ai, procurement@whitebirch.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Quick follow-up after demo — residency & hosting questions

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Magnus and I chatted and we want to make sure we pick the right hosting mode for our pilot. A couple of specific follow-ups: 

- Is Redwood Hosted API available with EU-only data residency for both inference and logs? We need both in-region storage for the pilot.
- If not, what is the minimum work to run on Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1? We want predictable latency and not cross-border token flows.
- For APAC users, can requests be routed to a different region without any data leaving EU for processing? We have a subset of users in APAC but cannot replicate full data residency there.

Also, procurement asked for a simple checklist of documentation (SOC2, data deletion policy, KMS options) and a pricing delta between Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC for a 3-month pilot.

Appreciate a short recap — Magnus and procurement are on a tight timeline.

Best,
Sofie
Head of Product, WhiteBirch AI

---

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sofie Berg <sofie@whitebirch.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, procurement@whitebirch.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — residency & hosting questions

Sofie — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise recap and next-step proposal so your procurement and infra teams can decide quickly.

1) Hosted API residency (EU-only):
- Short answer: Our hosted endpoint can be configured to process and persist inference outputs and logs in EU regions only, but that configuration is a Hosted+ feature (data residency controls) and depends on available region capacity. For a pilot we typically recommend Dedicated for strict in-region processing because it gives hardened routing and clear resource boundaries.

2) Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1:
- Provisioning time: ~5 business days for a pilot (subject to device availability).
- What you get: pinned GPU pool in eu-west-1, no cross-region routing for inference, optional KV-store in-region, and audit logs stored in your chosen EU bucket.

3) Cross-region routing for APAC:
- We can route APAC requests to an APAC endpoint, but if you require that all processed data remain in EU (e.g., for regulatory constraints), then routing APAC user traffic to EU processing is possible but will increase egress and latency; additionally, you must accept that APAC network transit occurs (we can provide traceroutes and latency profiles per PoP).
- If the requirement is that no data ever leaves EU under any circumstance, then APAC users must be served from an EU-only model — possible via Dedicated with a regional CDN for static assets, but this is unusual and requires explicit acceptance in the contract.

4) Docs & procurement checklist (attached):
- SOC 2 Type II report available (redacted).
- Data retention & deletion policy (attached).
- KMS options: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployments; for Hosted and Dedicated we support BYOK on request.

5) Pricing delta & timeline:
- Attached spreadsheet has ballpark monthly figures for a 3-month pilot. Short summary: Hosted (EU residency add-on) ~= $Xk/mo, Dedicated (reserved pilot pool) ~= Hosted + 70% premium, Private VPC/on-prem varies by infra. I asked Ben to include a clear line item.

Suggested next steps:
- Procurement: confirm required paperwork (SOC2 + DPA + KMS preference).
- Infra: confirm whether APAC traffic may be routed to EU or must remain local.
- Commercial: if you want guaranteed in-region processing, we lock in Dedicated for the pilot and provision eu-west-1 resources.

I attached a one-page residency matrix and a network diagram for the VPC option. Grace — can you add any technical counters about KV cache locality and log retention?

Regards,
Jonas
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: whitebirch-residency-matrix.pdf

---

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Sofie Berg <sofie@whitebirch.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — residency & hosting questions

Sofie / team — a couple of technical clarifications from infra: 

- KV cache: when Dedicated is pinned to eu-west-1 the KV cache and transformer execution remain in-region. That eliminates the typical prefix leak risk for EU-loc workflows.
- Logs: we can ship audit logs directly to your EU S3 bucket (or equivalent) with lifecycle rules; Redwood does not keep long-term copies unless explicitly configured.
- Networking for APAC: if you route APAC traffic to EU, requests traverse our edge PoPs and then the EU inference cluster. We can provide per-API-key routing rules if you want mixed routing per traffic type.
- VPC: the attached network diagram shows necessary customer VPC peering and recommended CIDR allocations for a pilot. We'll need firewall rules to allow TLS termination and mutual auth IP ranges.

If you confirm Dedicated, ops will start the provisioning checklist (IP whitelists, KMS token exchange, test dataset ingestion path).

Cheers,
Grace
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: networking-vpc-diagram.png

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: procurement@whitebirch.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — residency & hosting questions

Hi Sofie / Procurement —

Looping in the short pricing summary and procurement checklist. Highlights:
- We can provide a 3-month pilot discount on Dedicated for proof-of-value (details in attached spreadsheet).
- Required documents: executed DPA (we can send our template), SOC2 attestation, and a low-scope network intake form.
- For Private VPC/on-prem we require an SOW and lead time for on-site deployment planning (typically 6-8 weeks).

Action items for WhiteBirch procurement: please indicate KMS preference (Redwood-managed vs Customer-managed) and whether you need an indemnity clause for cross-border processing. If you prefer Dedicated, we'll estimate final pricing after you confirm expected qps and peak concurrency.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-2027.xlsx

From: Sofie Berg <sofie@whitebirch.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@whitebirch.ai, magnus@whitebirch.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — residency & hosting questions

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Quick confirmations before we close procurement: 

1) We will move forward with a 3-month Dedicated pilot in eu-west-1 (aiming to keep all inference & logs in EU). Please start provisioning checklist.
2) For APAC: we will accept routing APAC users to EU for the pilot but want latency profile numbers; if those don't meet our SLA we will explore a later APAC Dedicated pilot.
3) KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK) for the pilot.

Next meeting: please schedule a 30-minute provisioning kickoff with infra and procurement this week. Magnus will join.

Best,
Sofie
